policy.purpose: Store only decision-changing applicability constraints for trusted protocols used by Brali troubleshooters.
policy.source_rule: Every constraint must point to an exact eligibility or when-not-to-use statement in the protocol's Gold manual review. Validation fails if the source wording drifts.
policy.unknown_rule: Missing applicability metadata or unanswered required constraints never default to compatible.
policy.trust_rule: Only gold-ready protocols whose generated evidence state is reviewed or practical can enter a trusted troubleshooter.

constraints.question: For the next work block, can non-urgent interruptions wait until a sensible stopping point?
constraints.source_text: Do not use a focus timer where continuous monitoring, immediate responsiveness, driving, caregiving, safety-critical operations, or another duty makes deliberate disengagement inappropriate.

options.label: Yes — non-urgent interruptions can wait briefly.
No — I must stay immediately responsive.
options.reason: A deliberate focus boundary is a poor fit when the work requires immediate responsiveness.

constraints.question: Can you name one concrete, low-risk outcome for the next block?
constraints.source_text: The user has one concrete low-risk work or study outcome that can be advanced during a bounded focus block.

options.label: Yes — I know what should be different when the block ends.
Not yet — the task is still vague.
options.reason: This protocol needs one concrete outcome first. Define the next visible result before adding a timer.
